question: Is higher liver stiffness associated with thrombocytopenia in US adults?
refined_question: Among noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic (Age >=18 years), is greater liver stiffness (VCTE median) (per 5 kPa) associated with a higher prevalence of thrombocytopenia - platelets <150 x10^9/L, after adjustment for age, sex, race and ethnicity, income-to-poverty ratio, body mass index, diabetes (self-report, medication, or HbA1c >=6.5%), and smoking status?
title: Association of Liver Stiffness With Thrombocytopenia Among US Adults: NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic
hypothesis: Greater liver stiffness (VCTE median) is associated with a higher prevalence of thrombocytopenia - platelets <150 x10^9/L.

pico.population: noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic (Age >=18 years)
pico.comparator: Lower levels of the exposure (per-unit contrast; quartile 1 in sensitivity analysis)
pico.covariates: Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Body mass index, Diabetes (self-report, medication, or HbA1c >=6.5%), and Smoking status

model.rationale: Binary outcome: survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression with log link estimates prevalence ratios (PRs). PRs are preferred to odds ratios for cross-sectional data because ORs exaggerate associations when the outcome is common (>10%); the quasi-Poisson variance is robust under the design-based (Taylor linearization) estimator. Logistic regression is run as a sensitivity analysis.

adjustment_sets.label: Adjusted for age, sex, and race and ethnicity

missing_data.rationale: Complete-case primary analysis within the design; multiple imputation by chained equations as sensitivity analysis when covariates are missing.

sensitivity.label: Exclude heavy alcohol (>2 drinks/day men, >1 women)
Exclude self-reported hepatitis B or C
Exposure in weighted quartiles (Q4 vs Q1, P for trend)

rationale.statistician: Binary outcome: survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression with log link estimates prevalence ratios (PRs). PRs are preferred to odds ratios for cross-sectional data because ORs exaggerate associations when the outcome is common (>10%); the quasi-Poisson variance is robust under the design-based (Taylor linearization) estimator. Logistic regression is run as a sensitivity analysis.
rationale.epidemiologist: Covariates were selected as plausible common causes of liver stiffness (VCTE median) and thrombocytopenia - platelets <150 x10^9/L (minimal confounder set from the domain library): Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Body mass index, Diabetes (self-report, medication, or HbA1c >=6.5%), and Smoking status. Variables on the causal pathway or sharing laboratory components with the outcome/exposure are excluded to avoid over-adjustment.

limitations: Cross-sectional design: temporality cannot be established and associations must not be interpreted causally.
Single measurement of laboratory values; within-person variability and chronicity cannot be assessed.
Residual confounding by unmeasured or imperfectly measured factors (e.g., diet, medications, menstrual blood loss).
Self-reported comorbidities and behaviours are subject to recall and social-desirability bias.
NHANES excludes institutionalized and active-duty military populations.
